Fit the Smooth Block by Iterated Weighted Least Squares

Source: R/iwls.R
iwls_fit.Rd

Runs the scoring iteration on the objective of statmod_objective() at fixed hyperparameters, returning the coefficients and the history of the run.

Usage

iwls_fit(
  obj,
  start,
  method,
  n,
  pieces_at,
  verbose = FALSE,
  groups = NULL,
  frozen = integer(0),
  backup_at = NULL,
  damp_on_reject = TRUE,
  kinks_at = NULL,
  newton_at = NULL,
  switch_at = NULL,
  switch_after = Inf
)

Arguments

obj

The objective, as statmod_objective() returns it.

start

The starting coefficients, stacked into one numeric vector.

method

An Iwls() object, carrying the curvature, the solver, the budget and the stopping rule.

n

The number of observations, the divisor of the scaled stopping rule.

pieces_at

A function of the stacked coefficients returning what iwls_solve() needs, as iwls_pieces() builds it.

verbose

TRUE to print one line per iteration: the objective, the score per observation and the step length.

groups

A list of integer index vectors, one per equation, in the numbering of the coefficients handed in. NULL treats them as one group, which is right where the whole vector is being fitted.

frozen

Positions held at their starting values, an integer vector in the same numbering. They are dropped from every solve, so the run maximizes over the rest, and the stopping rule reads only the free coordinates, because the constrained optimum leaves in a held coordinate a score that does not vanish.

backup_at

NULL, or a function, like pieces_at, that builds the pieces on the expected information. The expected information takes the step where the observed step finds no acceptable point. An observed penalized information that is not positive definite is first repaired by pd_repair() and its step tried. A trial point whose objective raises an error is read as rejected. fit_smooth() passes one for a method that iwls_resolve() settled with the fallback.

damp_on_reject

Whether a line search that finds no acceptable step raises the Levenberg damping and retries (the default) or ends the run. fit_smooth() passes FALSE where the design carries a sharp break-point term, whose objective has a kink in the break-point at the observations: there every Gauss-Newton step from the minimum is rejected, and escalating the damping at every inner fit costs iterations without reaching anything that a stop would not.

kinks_at

NULL, or a function of the coefficients returning the rows of the linear constraints that hold the objective on its kinks there, a matrix with one column per coefficient, as kink_constraints() finds them. Where a line search rejects every step length, the problem is solved on the subspace that those constraints and frozen leave free (iwls_tied()); from the point reached one step on every coordinate is tried, and where it is rejected too the run stops there, with the verdict of the constrained fit.

newton_at

NULL, or a function of the coefficients returning the full Hessian of the objective, the scoring pieces' curvature plus the term that a block moving with its coefficients adds. Where the scoring step is rejected or shrunk below a tenth, the Newton step on it is tried by iwls_newton_step() and the one that decreases the objective more is taken.

switch_at

NULL, or a function, like pieces_at, that builds the pieces on the observed information. After switch_after iterations without convergence, or earlier when iwls_slow() reports a slow contraction of the score, it takes the place of pieces_at, and pieces_at that of backup_at. fit_smooth() passes one for a method that iwls_resolve() settled on the expected information from auto_info().

switch_after

The iteration after which switch_at replaces pieces_at.

Value

A list of ten: the six below; note, the reason for which a run stopped or NULL; aliased, the coordinates that the pivot left out; switched, the iteration at which the run moved to switch_at, or 0; and fallback, a named integer vector of four counts. The count indefinite is the number of iterations at which the observed penalized information was not positive definite, search the number at which the expected pieces stepped in for a step that found no acceptable point, error the number of trial points whose objective raised, and newton the number of iterations at which the Newton step on the full Hessian was taken in place of the scoring step. The six are:

par

the stacked coefficients reached, a numeric vector.

value

the penalized objective there, not averaged over the observations.

converged

a single logical: whether a stopping rule fired, including the dimensionless verdict.

iterations

the index of the iteration at which the loop ended. 1 means the rule was met at the first check, as a warm start already at the mode reports; the full step taken after the rule is met is not counted.

score

the score per observation at the point reached.

history

a data frame with one row per accepted step, or NULL when no step was accepted.

Repair of the curvature

A curvature that is not positive definite is repaired by flooring its eigenvalues, and the run continues. solve() would signal an error there and abandon a start that is merely far from the optimum.

The stopping rule

The built-in stopping rule compares a score divided by the sample size with tol, so that a threshold has the same meaning at \(n = 10\) and at \(n = 10^7\), and it also requires the Newton decrement to be at most \(10^{-6}\). After the rule is met, one more full step is taken. The objective itself is not averaged, because the penalty is added on that scale.

The dimensionless final verdict

The absolute score of a location equation carries the units \(1/y\). On a response three decades small its rounding floor sits above any fixed threshold, and a run stalled exactly at the optimum reads as a failure.

The verdict therefore includes a second, dimensionless reading, $$\max_j \lvert g_j \rvert / (n\,s_p), \qquad s_p = \sqrt{\mathrm{median}_j H_{jj} / n},$$ where \(s_p\) is taken over the equation to which each coordinate belongs.

It can relabel a run that has already stopped as converged, and it never stops a run that is still moving. Driving the loop with it would make the tolerance unreachable at the other end of the scale, where the magnitude of the objective grows with \(\log y\) and the stall guard fires first.

See also

iwls() for the settings, iwls_solve() for one step, iwls_score() for the dimensionless reading.
